title: Berlin Courtyards: Quick Summary
items: **Berlin's Höfe are hidden inner courtyards**, a legacy of the city's 1800s building boom. The best cluster sits around **Hackescher Markt**, where several beautiful ones stand within a ten-minute walk of each other.
**The walk is free and short.** From S Hackescher Markt to the Heckmann-Höfe is about **1.2 km across five courtyard stops**. You could rush it in half an hour, but it is built for slowing down.

**Start at the Hackesche Höfe** (Rosenthaler Straße 40): eight linked courtyards from 1906 and the largest complex in Germany. Walk past the famous tiled first courtyard and keep going, deeper toward Hof VIII.
**One door south is the opposite:** Haus Schwarzenberg (Rosenthaler Straße 39), a deliberately unrestored street-art passage that also holds the Anne Frank Zentrum and the Otto Weidt workshop museum.
**Then the quiet ones:** the Rosenhöfe (roses, wrought iron and a TV Tower view) and the courtyards off Sophienstraße, ending at the Heckmann-Höfe and its hand-made candy workshop.

**Go in the morning for calm.** Check the Bonbonmacherei's days before a special trip; it opens only a few days a week and takes a summer break. S Hackescher Markt: S3, S5, S7, S9 and trams M1, M4, M5, M6.
